subject: MAT
label: Grade 09
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 09 Mathematics, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 11 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Number systems
modules.outcome: work with rational and irrational numbers and laws of exponents
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Number systems', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: work with rational and irrational numbers and laws of exponents. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Show it with objects or a picture: build or draw the idea in 'Number systems' before using symbols.
Say the rule in your own words, then write one worked line, naming each step.
Use it: work with rational and irrational numbers and laws of exponents. Start with one easy question, then one with a real-life story.
Check it: use a second method, estimate, or work backwards to test your answer.
modules.example: Solved: Square root of 196: 14 x 14 = 196, so the root is 14. 2 cubed x 2 to the 4 = 2 to the 7 = 128. 0.75 = 3/4 is rational; the square root of 2 is not. Method: Model run for 'Number systems'. Read the question and underline what is asked. Draw or write what is known. Choose the method named in the unit. Work it line by line, one idea per line, with units where they apply. Estimate first so the answer can be tested for sense. Check by working backwards. What a good answer looks like: correct method, every step visible, units stated, and a one-line check.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Work with rational and irrational numbers and laws of exponents: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
